battle.name: 靈、宜、鹽、百之戰
battle.brief: 大曆八年（773）起，吐蕃軍自河西走廊東端向關內道推進，靈州、宜州、鹽州與百勝城一線告急。唐廷調三鎮節度使聯軍馳援，與吐蕃騎兵在黃河上游反覆拉鋸。靈州城頭的守軍靠弩機把攀城者壓在牆外，連弩正屬此類守城器械；本卡所配秦連弩早於本役千年，是這套守城火力體系的源頭。

kit.name: 秦連弩
kit.history: 弩機把拉力存起來，一踩一發。守城的一方靠它把攻城的人壓在牆外。

countries: 本役是唐代宗大曆年間唐蕃在黃河上游的一次大較量，交戰一方是唐朝關內道的邊軍系統，另一方是吐蕃王朝的河隴兵團。唐朝這一邊不是單一禁軍出動，而是以藩鎮節度使為骨幹的多路聯軍：總攬全局的是汾陽王郭子儀，他以尚書令、副元帥之尊總領河東、朔方軍務，並兼領河中，節制關內道上原與河套的兵馬；靈州、鹽州一線則由鄜坊、河中、昭義等節度使分道出師，沿黃河列營築城，節度使之間互不隸屬，遇敵須由中書門下調度才能協同。吐蕃一方以吐蕃王廷控制的河隴地區為基地，由論悉諾、尚結論一系的吐蕃名將統兵，騎兵為骨幹，輔以河湟、鄯廓的部族武力和隨軍家屬，糧秣靠馱畜自隨。雙方目標高度重疊：吐蕃要的是靈州這道黃河渡口與鹽州的鹽池，藉此把青海與河西連成一體；唐廷要保的是帝國西翼的門戶、鹽利與軍馬產地。所以一有接觸即成死戰，而全役最麻煩的一點，是唐軍各鎮互相觀望，集結往往比吐蕃出兵還慢。
countriesEn: This engagement was a major collision between the Tang and the Tibetan state on the upper Yellow River during the Dali era of Emperor Daizong. On one side stood the frontier command system of the Tang Guannei Circuit; on the other, the Tibetan armies drawn from the Heluo region under the Tibetan court. The Tang force was not a single imperial guard expedition but a coalition built on the backbone of regional military governors. The overall command was held by Guo Ziyi, Prince of Fenyang, who as Minister of Works and Vice Commander-in-Chief directed the armies of Hedong and Shuofang and also held the Hezhong command, overseeing the troops of the plateau and the Hetao plain beyond the Yellow River. Along the Lingzhou and Yanzhou line the troops came from separate circuits, the Fufang, Hezhong and Zhaoyi commands, each erecting its own camps along the river. Those governors were not subordinate to one another, and even a joint operation required the mediation of the central Secretariat. The Tibetan side drew its strength from the Heluo territories under Tibetan control, commanded by generals of the Lun and Shang clans such as Lun Sinuo and Shang Lun Jie, with cavalry as the core, supplemented by tribal levies and family followings from the Qinghai and Shannuo regions, and with all supplies carried on pack animals. The two sides wanted much the same thing: Tibet wanted the Yellow River crossing at Lingzhou and the salt pans of Yanzhou, in order to weld Qinghai and Hexi into a single corridor, while the Tang court wanted to hold the gateway of the empire's western flank, its salt revenues and its source of warhorses. Contact therefore turned at once into a fight to the death, and the gravest handicap for the Tang was that the circuits watched one another suspiciously, so that their armies usually took longer to concentrate than the Tibetans took to march.
people: 關於本役，漢文史料的記載相當零散，能確指姓名者有限，但大框架仍可勾出。唐方最高統帥是郭子儀：汾陽王、尚書令、副元帥，歷仕玄宗、代宗兩朝，出任河中、朔方統帥多年。他在河東的處置原則是不與吐蕃主力在荒野爭鋒，寧可退守城池、保全實力，也不肯把主力送出關口；本役初期唐軍的節制與後方調度，基本都出於這一思路。真正銜命前線、與吐蕃騎兵反覆接戰的，是河東猛將渾誠。此人出身胡族，相傳與吐渾舊族有淵源，勇力超眾，官拜將軍，長期跟隨郭子儀出塞，專司奔襲、追擊與斷糧一類的機動作戰；他在大曆年間的河東與河西戰線上屢建戰功，最終在大曆十五年前後的邊戰中病歿軍中，士卒為之舉哀。地方守將方面，靈州、鹽州一線的刺史與兵馬使姓名多已漫漶，僅留下據城固守、待援而戰的記載框架。吐蕃方面，統兵大將多以論氏、尚氏為號，論悉諾一系最為人知，長於騎射與縱隊奔襲，至於其統兵數目與進軍序列，漢籍記載不盡一致，諸說並存。真正決定本役節奏的，既非交戰雙方的將領，也不是某一場會戰，而是時間：吐蕃在唐軍尚未集結前已先取一城，節度使之間的互相推諉又令援軍遲滯，這才是全役迂迴反覆的關鍵。
peopleEn: Records of this engagement in the Chinese sources are scattered, and only a few names can be attached with certainty, yet the broad frame can still be drawn. The supreme Tang commander was Guo Ziyi, Prince of Fenyang, Minister of Works and Vice Commander-in-Chief, who served under both Xuanzong and Daizong and for many years commanded the Hezhong and Shuofang armies. His method on the Hedong front was to refuse a general engagement with the main Tibetan force on the open steppe: he would rather hold the cities and preserve his troops than march his main body out of the passes, and the initial disposition and logistics of the Tang army in this campaign followed that logic. The man who actually carried the fighting orders into contact with the Tibetan horse was Hun Cheng, a famous warrior of the Hedong army. He was of Hu extraction, tradition connecting his family with the old Tun-huan people, renowned for his strength, and for years he rode with Guo Ziyi on raids, pursuit and the cutting of supply lines. He won repeated successes on the Hedong and Hexi fronts in the Dali years and finally died of illness in camp during a frontier action around the fifteenth year of Dali, and the soldiers mourned him. As for the local commanders at Lingzhou and Yanzhou, the names of the prefects and of the officers commanding the troops have largely faded, leaving only the outline of a garrison that held its walls and waited for relief. On the Tibetan side the leading commanders were generally styled with the surnames of the Lun and Shang clans, of whom the line of Lun Sinuo is the best known; he excelled in mounted archery and in charge after charge at the gallop, though as to the size of his host and the order of his march the Chinese records do not agree, and say so openly. What really set the rhythm of this campaign was neither the commanders on either side nor any single pitched battle, but time: Tibet took a city before the Tang could concentrate, and the jockeying among the governors delayed the relief columns, and that, more than anything, explains the repeated seesaw of the whole campaign.
kits: 本卡所列的秦連弩並非本役的制式裝備：它屬戰國秦人已成熟的弩機技術，比大曆年間早了將近一千年。但在這條防線上，它的位置並不虛構——靈州、鹽州、百勝城這類邊城的守軍，靠的正是弩機這一套守城火力體系。弩與弓的分別在於以蹶張機把拉力存進機括，射手只須扣下懸機便可放矢，城頭的弩手不必像弓手那樣在每一次上弦時分心；本卡的連弩更把上弦與擊發連成一組，腳踏機括即可反覆發矢，射速遠勝單兵張弓，射界也能壓住城牆根一線的攀城者。與之並列的是唐軍常備的蹶張弩、擘張弩與床弩：床弩架在木牀或木架上，由數人合力張弦，矢大而遠，專射城下的撞車、雲梯與密集隊伍，弓手則負責近距補射與追擊散兵。攻城一方以游騎包抄為先，繼而以撞車、鈎拒、雲梯附牆，後方帶著大批家屬與畜群，準備長期圍城；守方的手段除弩砲之外，還有檑木礮石、拒馬與火桶，牆下挖塹、灌水、鋪拒馬刺，種種皆為常制。步騎的裝束仍是唐制：明光鎧與札甲為主，配長槍、陌刀與角弓，馬上用長槊與圓盾；吐蕃騎兵則以皮甲為主，弓箭、標槍與長刀，靠密集騎射與連續縱隊衝擊取勝，並不以攻城器械見長。這正是本役的關鍵：唐廷的長處在城防與火力，吐蕃的長處在機動力與騎射，雙方都無法單獨速決，靈、宜、鹽、百這幾座城才會在數年之間反覆易手。
kitsEn: The Qin repeating crossbow shown on this card was not a standard piece of equipment in this campaign: it belongs to the matured crossbow mechanism of the Warring States Qin, nearly a thousand years before the Dali era. Yet its place on this line is not imaginary, for the garrisons of frontier cities such as Lingzhou, Yanzhou and Baishengcheng relied on precisely this family of siege firepower. A crossbow differs from a bow in that a trigger mechanism stores the draw in the stock, and the shooter only needs to release the catch, so a crossbowman on the wall does not have to break his concentration each time the string is drawn. The repeating crossbow on this card links cocking and firing into a single motion, so that the trigger can be trodden to shoot again and again; its rate of fire far exceeds that of a single bowman, and its beaten zone can hold down the foot of the wall where the storming parties cling. Beside it stand the ordinary Tang arms: the tread-worked crossbow, the arm-braced crossbow and the bed crossbow. The bed crossbow rests on a wooden bed or frame, is cocked by several men at once, and shoots heavy arrows far beyond the reach of ordinary bows; it was aimed at the battering rams, the scaling ladders and the dense columns below the wall, while the archers behind supplied close-range shooting and the pursuit of broken men. The besiegers began with light cavalry working round the flanks, then brought up rams, hooked poles and scaling ladders against the wall, with masses of camp followers and herds behind them, prepared to sit down in a long siege. The defenders answered with crossbow stones, wooden beams, cheval-de-frise and fire-pots, with ditches dug under the wall, water poured into them and sharpened stakes laid in the approaches, all of it standard practice. The foot and horse remained Tang-pattern, with bright armour and lamellar plate, long spears, the miodao and composite bows, and on horseback the long lance and the round shield; the Tibetan cavalry fought in leather, with bow, javelin and long knife, winning by massed mounted archery and charge after charge, and they were no masters of siege engines. That is the crux of the campaign: the Tang were strong in walls and firepower, the Tibetans in mobility and horse-archery, and neither could force a decision alone, which is why Ling, Yi, Yan and Bai changed hands again and again across those years.
tactics: 本役的形態是攻城與反攻的拉鋸，而不是一次會戰。吐蕃方通常先以輕騎越過黃河冬日的冰面或淺灘，直插靈州與百勝城之間，切斷城與後方的聯繫；主力隨後列陣城下，或圍城，或攻略無城可恃的鹽州鹽池。守軍的部署是典型的唐代邊城體制：城頭分作數段，床弩置於高台俯射梯腳，蹶張弩與連弩在雉堞後依次待發，弓手在後排補漏；每有梯靠上牆，便以長鉤、撞竿把梯推倒，並以檑木礮石砸擊梯上攀登者。守方不輕易出城：一旦離開城牆的掩護，在開闊的寧夏平原上，任何步卒都會被吐蕃騎兵包抄吃掉，因此出擊多以短程突擊為主，出城數里、襲擾糧隊即回，或派小股游騎晝夜擾營，消耗敵方馬力與柴水。反攻時，唐軍多以河東、朔方騎兵為先鋒，逼近城寨後迫使吐蕃分兵，再以步軍列陣進逼，盡量避免在無遮蔽處被騎兵衝散；若無把握，寧可固守待援，等河西、隴右的援軍到齊再一併收復。糧道是這一役的另一條主線：靈州、鹽州的糧秣需由關中沿黃河與驛道北運，驢馬負載、牛車轉運是常規，一旦補給線被切斷，守軍往往在援兵抵達前就先耗盡箭矢與柴薪。
tacticsEn: The shape of this campaign was a see-saw of sieges and counter-attacks, not a single set-piece battle. The Tibetans normally began with light horse crossing the Yellow River over the winter ice or the shallows, driving in between Lingzhou and Baishengcheng to cut the cities off from their rear; the main body then came up in order before the walls, either investing a city or working against the salt pans of Yanzhou, which had no walls of its own to hold. The garrison was deployed in the classic Tang frontier manner: the wall was divided into several sections, the bed crossbows were set on high platforms to shoot down at the feet of the ladders, the tread crossbows and the repeating crossbows waited in turn behind the battlements, and the archers filled the gaps in the rear rank. Whenever a ladder was brought against the wall, long hooks and poles were used to push it back, and beams and stones were dropped onto the men still on it. The defenders did not lightly leave the city: once away from cover, on the open plain of Ningxia, any foot soldier would be enveloped and destroyed by the Tibetan horse, so the sorties were short, a few miles out, a raid on the baggage train and straight back, or else bands of light horse harried the camp day and night, wearing out the enemy's horses, firewood and water. In the counter-offensive the Tang habitually led with horse from Hedong and Shuofang, closing on the enemy positions to force the Tibetans to divide, then brought up foot in formation, careful never to be broken in the open by a charge; where there was no confidence, they chose to hold and wait, taking the garrisons back only when the reinforcements from Hexi and Longyou had all arrived. Supply was the other main line of the campaign: the grain and fodder of Lingzhou and Yanzhou had to be carried north from the Guanzhong plain along the Yellow River and the post roads, with donkeys and mules under load and ox-carts for the long haul, and once that line was cut the garrison would often run out of arrows and firewood before relief could reach it.
data: 本役可用的數字不多，以下幾項比較可靠。其一，靈州、鹽州同在黃河上游右岸（今寧夏吳忠、鹽池一帶），兩城相距不足百里，中間隔著鹽池與數處屯戍；宜州一帶的邊城具址諸說並存，一般考定在今甘肅靖遠至中衛一帶的黃河右岸。其二，自靈州至京師長安，陸路約一千三百公里，抵京須經坊、鄜等州，供應線極長；百勝城則是靈州西面的一處要塞城，與靈、鹽二州構成黃河上游的梯次。其三，鹽州以鹽池立州，唐廷的鹽利是財政的重要支柱之一，鹽池一失，歲入立刻受影響，這也是雙方都不肯罷手的原因之一。其四，弩的射程按當時通行的度量約在百步上下，床弩所射的矢大而重，一發的破甲力遠勝普通弓矢；相傳曹魏馬鈞曾改造連弩，令其一次預儲十數支箭矢連發，較單兵張弓省力數倍。其五，戰事自大曆八年（773）前後起，延續到大曆十五年（780）前後，前後約八年間，這一線城池數度易手，至吐蕃末年邊境局勢才有根本改變。至於雙方兵員，漢文史料只留下以萬計一類的概括，具體數目諸說並存且互相矛盾，本篇不採信任何一組確數；戰損、被俘與攻城器械的損耗數字，也多屬後人推估，不宜當作實錄。
dataEn: Few figures survive for this campaign, and the following are the more reliable ones. First, Lingzhou and Yanzhou both stand on the right bank of the upper Yellow River, in the Wuzhong and Yanchi area of present-day Ningxia, less than a hundred li apart, with the salt pans and several garrison posts between them. The exact site of the frontier towns of the Yi region is a matter of conflicting accounts, generally placed on the right bank of the Yellow River between Jingyuan and Zhongwei in present-day Gansu. Second, the overland distance from Lingzhou to the Tang capital of Chang'an is on the order of 1,300 kilometres, and the route ran through such prefectures as Fang and Fuo, so the line of supply was extremely long; Baishengcheng was a fortress town to the west of Lingzhou, and together with Ling and Yan it formed a stepped line on the upper river. Third, Yanzhou was established as a prefecture for its salt pans, and the salt revenues were one of the pillars of Tang finances; the loss of the pans would immediately have bitten into the state's income, which is one reason why neither side would disengage. Fourth, the effective range of the crossbow by the measures then in use was about a hundred paces, and the heavy arrow of the bed crossbow carried far more force against armour than an ordinary bowshot; it is said that Cao Wei's Ma Jun once rebuilt the repeating crossbow so that a single loading held a dozen or more arrows ready to be fired in succession, several times easier on the archer than a bow drawn by hand. Fifth, the fighting began around the eighth year of Dali, 773, and ran on until around the fifteenth year, 780; over roughly eight years these towns changed hands several times, and the frontier situation only altered fundamentally in the last years of the Tibetan state. As for the numbers of troops on each side, the Chinese records give only summaries of the order of tens of thousands; the precise figures conflict with one another, and no single set is accepted here. Losses, prisoners and the damage done to siege engines are likewise later reconstructions rather than record.
cause: 唐蕃之爭在河西走廊與青海一帶已延續百年，到大曆年間，老問題仍在兩處：吐蕃要向東取得青唐一帶的土地與牧場，唐朝的河西、隴右兩鎮則要保住通往西域的商路與馬場。大曆初年，唐廷在安史之亂後的混亂中一度裁撤節度使、合併軍鎮，邊防空虛，吐蕃趁隙奪取鄯、廓一帶，並把勢力推向靈州與鹽州。對吐蕃而言，靈州是黃河渡口與關內道的門戶，鹽州則是唐廷的鹽庫；拿下這兩處，等於在唐的西陲楔入一枚釘子，同時把青海與河西的通道連成一體，因此即使深入兵力不濟，吐蕃仍不惜長期圍城消耗。對唐廷而言，退讓的代價不只邊城：鹽利、京畿的馬匹與西部的驛道都在這一線；更麻煩的是，靈州、鹽州分屬不同節度使的轄境，遇敵時互相推諉，援軍集結往往比吐蕃出兵還慢。內部因素同樣不可忽視：代宗一朝藩鎮坐大，兵權與財賦多歸方鎮，中央對邊軍的調度時常打折。再加上吐蕃本身正處於向外擴張的頂峰，統合河隴與青海諸部的攻勢節奏很快，兩邊的碰撞就這樣在黃河上游形成。
causeEn: The Tang-Tibetan contest over the Hexi corridor and around Qinghai had already run for a century, and by the Dali years the old questions stood unchanged. Tibet wanted the land and pastures around Qingtang to the east, while the Tang circuits of Hexi and Longyou wanted to keep the trade road to the Western Regions and their horse pastures. In the early Dali years the court, still disordered after the An Lushan rebellion, had abolished military governors and merged commands, leaving the frontier thin; Tibet seized the chance to take Shannuo and Guozhou and pushed its strength towards Lingzhou and Yanzhou. For the Tibetans, Lingzhou was the crossing on the Yellow River and the gateway of the Guannei Circuit, and Yanzhou was the Tang salt depot; taking both would drive a spike into the western flank of the empire and join the corridors of Qinghai and Hexi into one road, and so even with limited strength pushed forward they were willing to sit in a long siege and wear the enemy down. For the Tang court the cost of giving ground went far beyond the frontier towns themselves, for the salt revenues, the horses of the capital districts and the western post road all lay on this line. More awkward still, Lingzhou and Yanzhou belonged to different commands, and when enemy raiding parties appeared each side would blame the other, so relief armies usually gathered more slowly than the Tibetans marched. Internal factors matter too: under Daizong the provincial commands grew strong, with troops and revenue increasingly in their hands, and the central dispatch of frontier troops was often a qualified business. At the same time the Tibetan state was at the height of its outward expansion, and the tempo of the offensive that united Heluo and the tribes of Qinghai was fast. The collision of the two was what took shape on the upper Yellow River.
impact: 這場戰爭的直接影響，是把唐廷的西部邊防重心由河西走廊進一步壓到黃河上游，並催生了一連串城防與屯田政策：靈州、鹽州一線的城寨被加固，軍屯與營田大幅擴張，鹽池周邊的水利灌溉被重新整治，寧夏平原從此成為關中最可靠的軍馬與糧食來源之一。對吐蕃而言，雖然一度跨過黃河，卻始終無法把靈、宜、鹽、百這條防線一口吞下；每次得手都必須分兵把守，反過來削弱了其在青海與河西的攻勢，雙方就這樣陷進誰也消滅不了誰的消耗局面。更深一層的影響是，隨著唐廷放棄死守西域、轉為固守關內的策略，吐蕃的戰略重心逐漸南移，河西走廊的商路與多個綠洲城邑相繼被切斷；但唐蕃之間的往來並未斷絕，邊市照常開放，俘虜與使節照樣往來，這種在刀兵之下的有限溝通，成為後來雙方各自調整策略的窗口。對後世而言，這條黃河防線上留下來的城址、烽燧與屯田痕跡，至今仍是研究唐代西北邊防格局最重要的實物之一。
impactEn: The direct effect of this war was to push the Tang court's western centre of defence further back from the Hexi corridor onto the upper Yellow River, and it produced a whole series of measures on fortification and garrison farming. The forts along the Lingzhou and Yanzhou line were reinforced, military and colonising farms were greatly extended, and the irrigation works around the salt pans were restored, so that the Ningxia plain became one of the most reliable sources of warhorses and grain for the Guanzhong core. For Tibet, though it crossed the Yellow River for a time, it never managed to swallow the Ling, Yi, Yan and Bai line in one bite; every gain had to be held by dividing the army, which in turn weakened its offensive in Qinghai and Hexi, and the two sides settled into a stalemate in which neither could destroy the other. At a deeper level, as the Tang abandoned the attempt to hold the Western Regions firmly and turned instead to defending the interior, the Tibetan strategic focus drifted south and the trade road through the Hexi corridor and a number of its oasis towns were cut off one after another. Yet intercourse between Tang and Tibet did not stop: the border markets opened as before, and prisoners and envoys travelled both ways, and this limited intercourse under the shadow of the sword became the window through which each side later adjusted its strategy. For later generations, the wall sites, beacon towers and traces of garrison farming left along this Yellow River line remain among the most important physical evidence for studying the structure of the Tang northwestern frontier.
result: 就本役的直接結果而言，雙方都沒有取得決定性的勝負。吐蕃一度攻入靈州、宜州，兵鋒直抵鹽州與百勝城下，逼得唐廷一度考慮放棄部分邊城；但在唐軍完成集結、河東與朔方援軍抵達之後，戰線又逐漸扭轉，靈、宜、鹽、百一線重歸唐軍手中，吐蕃退回河西與青海方向。此後數年，這幾座城仍在兩家之間反覆易手，直到大曆末年吐蕃攻勢轉弱，雙方才在黃河兩岸形成一條相對穩定的界線。戰役的結局之所以不乾淨，不在於某一役的勝負，而在於雙方戰略的極限：吐蕃能靠騎兵在寬闊地帶快速機動，卻難以長期攻下一座有弩有礮的邊城；唐朝能靠城牆與弩手守住防線，卻難以在缺水無草的荒漠上追上並殲滅對方騎兵。這類僵局往往只能靠時間解決：吐蕃王廷在其後數十年陷入王位繼承與內部爭鬥，直到九世紀中葉會昌前後，邊界局勢才真正改變；而唐廷守住河套，也等於保住了這個帝國最後的西翼。史料對本役的細節記載有限，諸說並存之處不少，上述判定只能以框架為準。
resultEn: As to the immediate outcome of the campaign, neither side won a decisive victory. Tibet did penetrate Lingzhou and the Yi region at one point, its spearhead reaching the walls of Yanzhou and Baishengcheng, and the Tang court at one moment entertained abandoning some of the frontier towns; but once the Tang forces had concentrated and the reinforcements from Hedong and Shuofang arrived, the line gradually turned, Ling, Yi, Yan and Bai returned to Tang hands, and the Tibetans withdrew towards Hexi and Qinghai. For several years afterwards these towns still changed hands between the two sides, and it was only when the Tibetan offensive waned in the closing years of the Dali era that a comparatively stable boundary was established on both banks of the Yellow River. The outcome is untidy not because of the result of any single engagement, but because of the limits of the two strategies. The Tibetans could move fast with horse across wide country, yet could not long hold down a frontier city furnished with crossbows and stone-throwers; the Tang could hold the line with walls and crossbowmen, yet could not run down and destroy an enemy horse in a desert without water or grass. Stalemates of this kind can only be resolved by time: the Tibetan court was drawn into struggles over succession and internal faction for the decades that followed, and only around the mid-ninth century, in the Huichang years, did the frontier situation genuinely change; and by holding the Hetao, the Tang kept, in the end, the last western wing of the empire. The surviving records of this campaign are thin and many points are disputed, so the judgements above can only be taken as the frame of what is known.
